The C2 code (with its two P1 fixes) is on branch feat/feed-retrieval-slice2b in the worktree at /work/dev/Code/git/Lumen/.claude/worktrees/feed-retrieval-slice2b, NOT yet committed. Both findings below were verified by the coordinator; fix them, do not re-litigate.

Work ONLY inside the worktree at /work/dev/Code/git/Lumen/.claude/worktrees/feed-retrieval-slice2b. Do NOT run git commit/push/add. Do NOT reinstall deps. Run gates from within pipeline/. Minimal, correct, no scope creep.

=== P2: the undefined->null coercion in record() is load-bearing but untested ===
FILE: pipeline/src/services/feed/trace.ts, record() (the `fullPayload === undefined ? null : fullPayload` coercion before writeJsonAtomic, ~line 142).
WHY IT MATTERS: the coercion stops record() from crashing when a caller passes an undefined payload (e.g. a synchronous spawn error throws before the client/adapter assigns tracePayload; record() then runs in the caller's finally with undefined). Without it, writeJsonAtomic -> JSON.stringify(undefined) -> writeFileSync(tmp, undefined) throws a TypeError that masks the real error. No existing test exercises this: reverting the coercion alone leaves every test green, so it is unguarded.
FIX: add a direct unit test in pipeline/test/trace.test.ts that calls the REAL createFeedTraceRecorder against a temp run dir with `record(call, undefined)` and asserts (a) it does NOT throw, (b) the payload file on disk is `null` (JSON), and (c) the returned FeedCallTrace has a valid payload_path. Prove it is non-tautological: revert the coercion, watch THIS test fail with the TypeError, then restore. Do not weaken the coercion.

=== P3: the client fabricates a result summary on failed calls ===
FILE: pipeline/src/services/feed/feedq-retrieve-client.ts, run() finally (~line 262, the `result: summarizeResult(command, tracePayload)` spread).
THE BUG: the P1 fix made tracePayload a defined diagnostic object ({status,stderr} etc.) on error branches. The finally's condition `tracePayload !== undefined` is now true on failures, so it calls summarizeResult(command, diagnostic). summarizeResult casts the diagnostic to a FeedRetrieveResponse; hits/coverage are undefined, so it emits `result: { hit_refs: [], coverage_incomplete: [] }` for a call that FAILED -- which reads as "0 hits, complete coverage" and poisons the D2B-6 failure-analysis / eval-mining data. The feedq-adapter.ts path already guards this (it only emits result when the parsed response's count/total are defined); the client must match.
FIX: emit `result` only on success. Guard it on `traceError === null` (the success path is the only one with a real, summarizable payload), matching the adapter's guard. A failed call records error + the verbatim diagnostic payload at payload_path and NO fabricated result field. Add/extend a test in pipeline/test/feedq-retrieve-client.test.ts asserting a failed retrieve/deref call's recorded FeedCallTrace has `result` undefined (not a zero-hit summary) while error is set. Non-tautological.

CONSTRAINTS: touch only trace.ts, feedq-retrieve-client.ts, and their test files. No consumer-step code, no legacy, no dead code. Keep any doc comments honest.

GATES to run and report verbatim:
- (cd /work/dev/Code/git/Lumen/.claude/worktrees/feed-retrieval-slice2b/pipeline && npx tsc --project tsconfig.typecheck.json)
- (cd /work/dev/Code/git/Lumen/.claude/worktrees/feed-retrieval-slice2b/pipeline && npx vitest run test/trace.test.ts test/feedq-retrieve-client.test.ts test/feedq-adapter.test.ts)
- Confirm the full suite stays at exactly 58 pre-existing failures, zero new: (cd /work/dev/Code/git/Lumen/.claude/worktrees/feed-retrieval-slice2b/pipeline && npx vitest run) -- report the failed/passed/skipped counts.

Return: a one-paragraph description of each fix (p2CoercionTest, p3ResultGuard), the gate commands with pass/fail and key output, and any deviations.
